Chapter 1: What Are We Actually Building?
Before writing a single line of code, you need to understand the full picture.
that lives entirely on your phone. It has no subscription fee, no internet requirement (after setup), and no data leaving your device.
When you open the app, you see a menu:
You either tap a mode or speak its name. The app opens that mode and you have a conversation. The AI remembers what you said during the session.
The Two Parts Of The System
Think of it like a restaurant:
│ • What you see • The AI brain │
│ Built in: Kotlin Built in: Python │
│ They talk via: HTTP on localhost:8000 │

The Android app (Kotlin) is what you see and touch. The Python backend is the brain running silently in Termux. They talk to each other over a local connection — like two apps on the same phone whispering to each other.

You might wonder: "Why not put everything in Kotlin?" The answer is simple — your AI models, ChromaDB, PDF tools, and all the agent logic are already written in Python and proven to work on your phone. Rewriting all of that in Kotlin would take 10x longer and be harder to maintain. Instead, we wrap a professional UI around the Python brain you already have.

This is one of the most important concepts in Kotlin. In many other languages, your app can crash because a variable is

// In Kotlin, by DEFAULT, nothing can be null:

val length = userInput?.length // ✅ Returns null if userInput is null, doesn't crash
// With a default value if null:

Every Activity goes through these stages. Understanding them prevents bugs:
User opens app → onCreate() → Setup UI, find views, set listeners
App becomes visible → onStart() → Good place to start animations
User can interact → onResume() → App is in foreground, fully active
User gets a call → onPause() → Save data, pause things
App goes to background → onStop() → Stop heavy work
User kills app → onDestroy() → Clean up everything
